title: Metering drain bridge for late-arrival token reconciliation and idempotent replay
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Regional edge nodes and third-party ingestion endpoints are producing late-arriving token records (out-of-order events, replays, and delayed logs) that currently either get dropped or surface as duplicate/mismatched entries in the tenant billing ledger. This causes transient invoice spikes and manual investigation for affected customers.

Goal: Build a "drain bridge" service that consumes late-arrival token events from the existing dead-letter / late-events Kafka topic, normalizes and deduplicates them, and replays reconciled events into the canonical metering ledger in an idempotent, shard-aware manner while preserving provenance metadata. The service must operate with bounded memory, provide replay guarantees, and be safe to run in parallel with existing ingestion pipelines (shadow mode first).

Design summary:
- Input: Kafka topic "tokens.late.v1" (partitioned by tenant_id). Events include original_event_id, ingestion_timestamp, raw_token_count, route, model_variant, source_shard, and provenance metadata.
- Core components:
  - Per-tenant windowed aggregator (Tumbling/Session-style) that groups late events by original request id + timestamp tolerance.
  - Idempotency key creation using stable (tenant, request_id, canonicalized-route, event_hash).
  - Shard-aware sequencer that attaches a reconciliation sequence number for ordering; uses a lease over a lightweight Redis slot for parallel safety.
  - Replay writer that writes reconciled rows into ledger-write API / ledger-reconcile endpoint, using upsert semantics and conditional compare-and-swap on the ledger_namespace / reconciliation_version.
  - Anti-entropy checker that cross-validates ledger state against raw source logs for a random sample of tenants daily.
- Failure semantics: The drain bridge must be able to restart safely, resume from offsets, and backpressure Kafka (avoid OOM on burst of late events).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Shadow mode: The service can run in production in shadow mode (no writes) and produce a reconciliation plan for 95% of late events for a 30-day period without increasing error rates downstream.
2) Idempotent writes: Replayed events must not create duplicate ledger entries; verify by synthetic tests and production sampling.
3) Latency SLA: Reconciliations for late events arrive within 48 hours of event ingestion for 99% of cases when retention policy allows.
4) Observability: Per-tenant reconciliation rate, false-positive dedup rate, and write failures surfaced to existing console dashboards.
5) No invoice regressions in controlled canary tenants (0 customer-impacting billing deltas beyond expected correction windows).

Implementation tasks (high level):
- T1: Schema definition and validation for tokens.late.v1 (Avro changes documented)
- T2: Lightweight Go service prototype with per-partition consumer and windowed aggregator
- T3: Redis slotting and sequencer library (with integration tests)
- T4: Ledger reconcile API extension to accept reconciliation metadata (PR in https://github.com/redwood-inference/ledger/pull/2437)
- T5: Shadow-run harness and dashboards (Prometheus metrics + Console route)
- T6: Canary rollout and billing reconciliation runbook

Dependencies:
- Kafka retention configuration change for tokens.late.v1 (ENG-224881 - ops task)
- Ledger transactional upsert endpoint (see PR linked above)
- Small Redis cluster for sequencing (ops ticket pending)

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for idempotency key generation and upsert collision resolution.
- Integration tests in staging with synthetic late-event generator covering reordering and dupe scenarios.
- Backfill dry-run on a 7-day historical sample in staging to validate reconciliation decisions.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge feature flags and run in shadow mode in production for 2 weeks, monitor metrics.
2) Enable for 5 low-impact tenants (opt-in) with daily manual review of reconciliations for 1 week.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% tenant sample; monitor billing deltas and false positives.
4) Full enable with automatic correction and anti-entropy verification after 6 weeks.

Rollback: Feature flag can disable replay writer immediately; reconciliation effects are implemented as upserts with versioning so a rollback job can re-evaluate changes and mark corrections as reversed if needed.

Runbook links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Drain+Bridge+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/drain-bridge/pull/12
- Staging dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/late-token-reconciler

Notes/risks:
- Risk: High memory pressure if tenants flood late events—mitigation: per-tenant soft limits and spill-to-disk policy.
- Risk: Incorrect idempotency algorithm could mask real usage corrections—mitigation: sampled manual review and audit logs with provenance.
- Ops: Requires coordination with infra for Redis and Kafka retention changes.
